You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. data.finalText:
I'll read the file first, then make the edit.
The hook `guard-no-physical-targets` blocked the edit, and I made no changes. Its message was:

> Blocked by guard-no-physical-targets: the write to /mnt/d/KERJA/PT AGS/RnD/Hackathon/Kirowen_2026/ghostwire/csharp/GhostWire/Modbus.cs adds a network target outside the loopback simulator.
> - line 4: non-loopback IPv4 literal 192.168.1.50
> GhostWire must connect only to IPAddress.Loopback and simulator-owned ports (see .kiro/steering/safety.md). Remove the literal or the request-controlled host and retry.

GhostWire refuses this because `192.168.1.50` is a non-loopback address, and the safety rules allow the client to connect only to `IPAddress.Loopback` and ports owned by its own simulators. A hardcoded plant gateway address would put a possible real-equipment target into the code, and the lab is meant to be simulation-only.
